translationRepairs: Gaozu, temple name the Sagely, Literary, Martial, Virtuous, and Filial Emperor, was born to Niezhji. The family sprang from western tribes; they left the Zhuye for Tang service and settled with them in the Yin Mountains.

Gaozu, the Sagely, Literary, Martial, Virtuous, and Filial Emperor, was born to Niezhji. The family sprang from western tribes; they left the Zhuye for Tang service and settled with them in the Yin Mountains.

Focus unit opens 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝: 高祖 alone is the temple name, and 聖文章武明德孝皇帝 is the posthumous honorific. Labeling that title “temple name” is wrong; the proposed wording drops the mislabel while keeping the rest intact.
Yan caught the column before it could form. Jingtang led barely a dozen riders in a slashing charge, took Yan prisoner, and broke clear.
Yan caught the column before it could form. Jingtang led barely a dozen riders in a slashing charge, brought Zhuangzong out, and broke clear.

After 為掞所掩, 敬瑭…取之以旋 names no capture of Liu Yan; the next unit has 莊宗拊其背 praising Jingtang, so 之 is the endangered Zhuangzong. “Took Yan prisoner” invents an unstated capture; “brought Zhuangzong out” matches the rescue sense.
Early in the second year, on guihai of the first month, Lu Wenzhi of Anyuan defected to Wu.
Early in the second year, on guihai of the first month, Lu Wenjin of Anyuan defected to Wu.
Focus unit names 盧文進; 文進 is Wenjin, not Wenzhi. The proposed idiomatic name corrects that reading error without other changes.
In spring of year 2, on guihai the first day of the first month, Lu Wenzhi, military governor of Anyuan, rebelled and surrendered to Wu.
In spring of year 2, on guihai the first day of the first month, Lu Wenjin, military governor of Anyuan, rebelled and surrendered to Wu.
The same 盧文進 in the focus unit requires Lu Wenjin in the literal field; replacing Wenzhi restores the Chinese personal name.
Wang Yanchong, Lingzhou garrison commander, seized Huaiyuan and rose in revolt.
Wang Yanzhong, Lingzhou garrison commander, seized Huaiyuan and rose in revolt.
Focus unit has 王彥忠; 忠 is zhong, so Yanchong misreads the given name. Wang Yanzhong is the correct reading.
Wang Yanchong, garrison commander at Lingzhou, rebelled holding Huaiyuan city.
Wang Yanzhong, garrison commander at Lingzhou, rebelled while holding Huaiyuan city.
Literal English likewise misreads 彥忠 as Yanchong; Yanzhong matches 王彥忠, and “rebelled while holding Huaiyuan city” still renders 以懷遠城反.
On jiwei Yanchong submitted; Palace Attendant officer Qi Yanzuo then slew him.
On jiwei Yanzhong submitted; Palace Attendant officer Qi Yanzuo then slew him.
Short form 彥忠 in this unit is the same person as 王彥忠 in s0117; idiomatic Yanchong must be Yanzhong.
On jiwei Yanchong surrendered; Palace Attendant officer Qi Yanzuo killed him.
On jiwei Yanzhong surrendered; Palace Attendant officer Qi Yanzuo killed him.
Literal 彥忠 likewise requires Yanzhong to match the preceding 王彥忠; the rest of the surrender wording is already accurate.
Western tribes struck Jing; Zhang Yanzhe of Zhangyi drove them off and took their chief Yeliluoxiadú prisoner.
Western tribes struck Jing; Zhang Yanze of Zhangyi drove them off and took their chief Yeliluoxiadú prisoner.
Focus unit names 張彥澤; 澤 is ze, so Yanzhe is a wrong reading. Zhang Yanze restores the Chinese personal name.
Western barbarians raided Jing; Zhang Yanzhe, military governor of Zhangyi, defeated them and captured their leader Yeliluoxiadú.
Western barbarians raided Jing; Zhang Yanze, military governor of Zhangyi, defeated them and captured their leader Yeliluoxiadú.
The literal field has the same 張彥澤 misread as Yanzhe; correcting to Yanze matches the Chinese without changing the rest.
On yihai of the eleventh month shrines to Tang Gaozu, Taizong, Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and the Deposed Emperor were raised in the Western Capital.
On yihai of the eleventh month shrines to Tang Gaozu, Taizong, Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min were raised in the Western Capital.
Focus unit lists 湣帝 among the Tang emperors honored; that is Emperor Min (Mindi), not the Deposed Emperor (廢帝, Congke). “Emperor Min” restores the correct identity.
In the eleventh month of winter, on yihai, temples to Tang Gaozu, Taizong, Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and the Deposed Emperor were established in the Western Capital.
In the eleventh month of winter, on yihai, temples to Tang Gaozu, Taizong, Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min were established in the Western Capital.
Literal English likewise renders 湣帝 as the Deposed Emperor; Emperor Min matches 湣帝 and distinguishes him from Congke.
On dingmao of the ninth month He Ning, Hanlin director and vice minister of revenue, entered the Chancellery as co-grand councilor.
On dingmao of the ninth month He Ning, Hanlin director and vice minister of revenue, became vice director of the Secretariat and co-grand councilor.
He Ning is appointed 中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事: 中書侍郎 is vice director of the Secretariat, not entry into the Chancellery. The proposed wording restores both the office and the co-grand councilorship.
In the ninth month, on dingmao, He Ning, Hanlin academician in charge and vice minister of revenue, became vice director of the Chancellery and co-grand councilor.
In the ninth month, on dingmao, He Ning, Hanlin academician in charge and vice minister of revenue, became vice director of the Secretariat and co-grand councilor.
Literal “vice director of the Chancellery” misassigns 中書侍郎; Secretariat is required, matching the Chinese office title.
On wuyin of the first month in the sixth year Tang Shuyu was made Prince of Xing’an and Tailu Duke of Changning.
On wuyin of the first month in the sixth year Tang Shuyu was made Prince of Xing’an and Tailu as Duke of Changning.
Chinese 封唐叔虞為興安王，臺駘為昌寧公 enfeoffs two recipients in parallel. Without “as” before Duke of Changning, Tailu can fuse into Tang Shuyu’s titles; inserting “as” restores the two separate grants.
